blueprint.source: CDS Paper II General Knowledge: 120 questions, 100 marks, 2 hours; negative 1/3.

questions.text: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at Kanpur?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Map leaders to centers. Lakshmibai -> Jhansi; Zafar -> Delhi; Kunwar Singh -> Bihar/Arrah. By elimination, Nana Sahib leads at Kanpur. Full Solution: Nana Sahib (Dhondu Pant), the adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II, led the sepoys at Kanpur along with his commander Tantia Tope. The siege of Wheeler's entrenchment and the subsequent massacre at Satichaura Ghat are key events associated with this center.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian wetlands is currently listed under the Montreux Record?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Know the status. Chilika was *removed* from the Record in 2002 (restoration success). Keoladeo and Loktak are the two Indian sites *currently* on it. Wular and Sambhar are Ramsar sites but not on Montreux Record. Full Solution: The Montreux Record is a register of Ramsar sites where ecological changes have occurred. Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan) was placed on the record in 1990 due to water shortage and invasive species. Chilika Lake was removed in 2002 after successful restoration.

questions.text: The Battle of Buxar fought in 1764 was a decisive victory for the British East India Company over the combined forces of which three rulers?

options.label: A
options.text: Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah, and Shah Alam II

options.label: B
options.text: Siraj-ud-Daulah, Mir Jafar, and Shah Alam II

options.label: D
options.text: Haidar Ali, Tipu Sultan, and Nizam of Hyderabad

questions.solution: Shortcut: Buxar (1764) follows Plassey (1757); the coalition was the Nawab of Bengal (Mir Qasim), Nawab of Awadh (Shuja-ud-Daulah), and Mughal Emperor (Shah Alam II). Eliminate options with Siraj-ud-Daulah (died 1757) or South Indian rulers. Step-by-step: The battle ended with the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), granting Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa to the Company.

questions.text: Which vitamin is synthesized by the human skin when exposed to ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation from sunlight?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Vitamin D is uniquely called the 'Sunshine Vitamin'; it is synthesized from 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin. Vitamins A, B12, and C are essential dietary nutrients not produced by sun exposure. Full: UVB radiation (290–315 nm) converts cutaneous 7-dehydrocholesterol to pre-vitamin D3, which isomerizes to Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol), later hydroxylated in liver and kidney to active form.

questions.text: Which of the following Peninsular rivers forms a delta on the east coast instead of an estuary on the west coast?
questions.solution: Shortcut: West-flowing rivers (Narmada, Tapi, Mahi, Sabarmati) form estuaries; East-flowing rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) form deltas. Godavari is the only east-flowing river listed. Full: The Godavari rises in Maharashtra and drains into the Bay of Bengal, forming a large, fertile delta, unlike the west-flowing rivers which enter the Arabian Sea via estuaries.

questions.text: The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India contains provisions regarding which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes

options.label: B
options.text: The Union List, State List, and Concurrent List

options.label: C
options.text: The list of official languages of the Republic of India

options.label: D
options.text: Forms of Oaths or Affirmations for public officials

questions.solution: Shortcut (Option Elimination): Memorize the 'Big 6' Schedules: 3rd (Oaths), 7th (Centre-State Lists), 8th (Languages), 9th (Validation of Acts), 10th (Anti-Defection), 11th (Panchayats). Option A is 5th Schedule, Option C is 8th Schedule, Option D is 3rd Schedule. Only Option B matches the 7th Schedule. Step-by-step: The 7th Schedule under Article 246 defines the legislative competence of Parliament and State Legislatures through three lists: Union List (List I - 97 subjects originally), State List (List II - 66 subjects originally), and Concurrent List (List III - 47 subjects originally).

questions.text: Malaria in humans is caused by protozoan parasites of the genus Plasmodium. Which of the following species is responsible for the most severe and fatal form of malaria (cerebral malaria)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Falciparum' sounds like 'Fatal'; it causes malignant/cerebral malaria. Vivax/Ovale cause relapsing malaria (hypnozoites); Malariae causes quartan malaria. Step-by-step: P. falciparum infects RBCs of all ages, leading to high parasitemia, cytoadherence in brain capillaries (cerebral malaria), and highest mortality.

questions.text: Under which Article of the Constitution of India is the Finance Commission constituted?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Memorize key fiscal Articles: Art 280 (Finance Commission), Art 279A (GST Council), Art 110 (Money Bill), Art 265 (Tax authority). Eliminate 279A (GST), 110 (Money Bill), 265 (Tax levy). Full: Article 280 mandates the President to constitute a Finance Commission every five years to recommend distribution of tax revenues between Union and States.

questions.text: The First Five Year Plan in India was launched for the period:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate 1947 (Independence), 1950 (Planning Commission formed), 1952 (First General Elections). The Plan commenced April 1, 1951. Full Solution: The Planning Commission was established in March 1950. The First Five Year Plan (based on the Harrod-Domar model) was presented in Parliament in December 1951 and covered the period 1951-1956, focusing primarily on agriculture and irrigation.

questions.text: The event 'Dharmachakra Pravartana' (Turning of the Wheel of Law) in Buddhism refers to Buddha's first sermon delivered at:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the pilgrimage sequence 'L-B-S-K': Lumbini (Birth), Bodh Gaya (Enlightenment), Sarnath (First Sermon/Dharmachakra Pravartana), Kushinagar (Mahaparinirvana). Full: After attaining enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, Buddha travelled to the Deer Park at Sarnath (near Varanasi) where he delivered his first sermon to five ascetics, setting the Wheel of Dhamma in motion.

questions.text: The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog) was established by a resolution of the Union Cabinet on which date, replacing the Planning Commission?
questions.solution: Shortcut: NITI Aayog started with the New Year 2015 (Jan 1). Planning Commission was established March 1950. Step-by-step: The Government replaced the 65-year-old Planning Commission with NITI Aayog via Cabinet Resolution on Jan 1, 2015. It serves as a policy think tank with the PM as Chairperson, promoting cooperative federalism.

questions.text: The 'Agni-V' ballistic missile developed by DRDO is categorized as an:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Agni series range progression: Agni-I/II (MRBM ~2000km), Agni-III (IRBM ~3500km), Agni-IV (IRBM ~4000km), Agni-V (ICBM >5000km). ICBM threshold is 5500km. Full: Agni-V is a three-stage, solid-fuelled, road-mobile ICBM with a strike range of 5,000–8,000 km, capable of carrying MIRV warheads, placing India in the elite ICBM club.

questions.text: Which writ is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to review a judicial decision?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use meaning elimination. Habeas Corpus = 'Produce the body' (detention); Mandamus = 'We command' (duty); Quo Warranto = 'By what authority' (office). Certiorari = 'To be certified' (review). Full Solution: Certiorari is a curative writ issued by the Supreme Court or High Courts to review a decision of a lower court, tribunal, or quasi-judicial body. It ensures judicial decisions are within jurisdiction and follow natural justice.

questions.text: Which of the following Peninsular rivers flows through a rift valley and forms an estuary on the west coast instead of a delta?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Only Narmada and Tapi (Tapti) flow West through rift valleys forming estuaries; all others (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) flow East forming deltas. Step-by-step: Narmada originates from Amarkantak, flows west through a rift valley between Vindhya and Satpura ranges, and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat forming an estuary.

questions.text: Which of the following is the highest mountain peak in India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate Kanchenjunga (3rd highest globally but highest *entirely within* India), Nanda Devi (23rd highest), and Kamet. K2 is the highest peak on the Survey of India maps. Full Solution: K2 (8,611 m), located in the Karakoram Range (Pakistan-occupied Kashmir), is officially recognized by the Survey of India as the highest peak in India. Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) is the highest peak located entirely within Indian territory.
